For q a prime power≥2, F=F_(q²), K=F_(q6), every F-rational line meeting the Hermitian surface without being a generator has only F-rational intersection points, so U has no degrees one or two. Three q²-Frobenius conjugates of a degree-three point on U span a unique F-plane; their Hermitian Gram matrix is nonsingular, since vanishing cyclic pairing would force a totally isotropic 3-space in rank4. Normalize the nonzero c=Σv_j^(q³+1) via the K/F_(q³) norm, descend the frame isometry and extend by a Hermitian-line isometry, proving PGU(4,q) transitivity. Stabilizers are (μ_(q³+1)×μ_(q+1))/μ_(q+1)≅μ_(q³+1), giving #U(K)=q6(q²−1)(q4−1) and canonical smooth-section fibers. Extension counts and zeta use classical Hermitian point/line data, not a new cohomology proof. Fresh GF64 arithmetic counted 45 rank1,1620 rank2,2880 rank3 projective Hermitian points as expected; finite q=2 does not prove all q.
